dossierSummary: Regulation (EU) No 1215/2012 on jurisdiction and recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters (recast) provides a stable and predictable framework for businesses and consumers in cross-border disputes through uniform rules on jurisdiction, recognition, and enforcement of judgments within the EU in civil and commercial matters. The report on its application concluded that it has been effective overall but identified the need for targeted updates to simplify, modernize, clarify its provisions through a formal review.

publications.title: Public consultation on the possible revision of Regulation (EU) No 1215/2012

publicationTranslations.value: The consultation is open to all stakeholders, such as individuals, businesses (including SMEs), legal practitioners, national authorities (particularly courts applying the Regulation), EU and national consumer associations, business associations and academic experts.

The aim of the consultation is to collect evidence, experiences and opinions from relevant stakeholders. These contributions will inform the analysis and assessment of the performance of the Regulation in its current form, the shortcomings identified, possible policy options to address them and their expected impacts.

initiativeTranslations.value: Jurisdiction rules and recognition and enforcement of judgments – Brussels Ia Regulation (review)

Regulation (EU) No 1215/2012 sets out uniform rules on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in the EU in civil and commercial matters, providing a stable and predictable framework for businesses and consumers in cross-border disputes.

This initiative aims to conduct a formal review of the Regulation. In particular, it aims to implement targeted updates to simplify, modernise and clarify the Regulation, as recommended in a recent report on its application.
